value: A positively charged nucleus at the centre of the atom
reasoning: In Rutherford's experiment most alpha particles passed straight through the foil but a very small fraction rebounded through large angles, which can only happen if the atom's positive charge and almost all its mass are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus.

Isobars are nuclides with the same mass number but different atomic numbers; argon-40 (Z = 18) and calcium-40 (Z = 20) both have mass number 40, whereas the other pairs share an atomic number and are isotopes.

value: Copper displacing lead from lead chloride
reasoning: A metal can displace only a less reactive metal from its salt, and copper lies below lead in the reactivity series, so copper cannot displace lead; iron, zinc and magnesium all lie above copper and displace it from copper sulphate.

The pH scale runs from 0 to 14 with 7 neutral, and pH falls as hydrogen-ion concentration rises, so pH 0 corresponds to a hydrogen-ion concentration of 1 mol per litre, the acidic extreme of the scale.
The parietal cells of the gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid, which makes the stomach contents strongly acidic, kills ingested microbes and activates pepsinogen into pepsin.

value: Boric acid-antiseptic, citric acid-food preservative, magnesium hydroxide-antacid, acetic acid-pickle
reasoning: Boric acid is a mild antiseptic used in eyewash, citric acid acts as a food preservative and acidity regulator, magnesium hydroxide is milk of magnesia used as an antacid, and acetic acid as vinegar is the preserving medium in pickles.
Pitch is the perception of how shrill or flat a sound is and rises with the number of vibrations per second, so it is decided by frequency, while amplitude decides loudness.

value: That X-rays are deflected by electric fields (they are not)
reasoning: X-rays are electrically neutral electromagnetic waves, so neither electric nor magnetic fields deflect them; the remaining statements about their high penetrating power and very short wavelength are all correct.

value: That the image is real (a plane mirror forms a virtual image)
reasoning: Rays reflected from a plane mirror only appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror and never actually meet there, so the image is virtual, erect, laterally inverted, of the same size and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

A periscope uses two plane mirrors fixed at opposite ends of a tube, each tilted at 45 degrees to the tube's axis and therefore parallel to one another, so light entering horizontally is turned down and then back to the horizontal at the eyepiece.
Refractive index is the ratio of the speed of light in air to that in the medium, so dividing 3 x 10^8 metres per second by 3/2 gives 2 x 10^8 metres per second.

Along the electromagnetic spectrum wavelength decreases from radio waves through infrared and visible light to ultraviolet, so of the four listed the ultraviolet radiation has the shortest wavelength.
Hooke's law gives restoring force as the force constant times the extension, so the force constant is force divided by length and is measured in newton per metre.

An epidemic spreads rapidly through a population in a short time, as cholera, malaria and smallpox outbreaks do, whereas elephantiasis is a slowly developing chronic filarial condition that appears only after years of repeated infection and so is endemic rather than epidemic.

Amphibians such as the salamander have a heart of two atria and a single ventricle; the shark Scoliodon has a two-chambered heart while birds and mammals such as the pigeon and human have four chambers.

value: Pollination, fertilization, division of zygote, formation of embryo, seedling
reasoning: Pollen must first reach the stigma, then the male gamete fuses with the egg to form a zygote, which divides to build the embryo inside the seed, and only on germination does the seedling appear.
Exhaled air is rich in carbon dioxide, which reacts with calcium hydroxide in limewater to form insoluble calcium carbonate, and it is this white precipitate that makes the solution milky.
ATP is called the energy currency of the cell because the energy released by respiration is stored in its terminal phosphate bond and is spent directly to drive contraction, transport and synthesis.

Digestion begins in the buccal cavity where saliva mixes with food, and salivary amylase acting on starch is therefore the first enzyme food meets, well before pepsin in the stomach or trypsin in the small intestine.
The Dandi March of 1930 was a protest against the British salt monopoly and tax, and Gandhi broke the law by preparing salt, that is sodium chloride, from sea water at Dandi.

value: Bleaching powder-CaOCl2, baking soda-NaHCO3, washing soda-Na2CO3.10H2O, slaked lime-Ca(OH)2
reasoning: Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, washing soda is the decahydrate of sodium carbonate, and slaked lime is calcium hydroxide obtained by adding water to quicklime.
Blue vitriol is copper sulphate pentahydrate, in which five molecules of water of crystallisation are associated with each formula unit and whose loss on heating turns the crystals white.

value: Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in air to form a coating of silver sulphide
reasoning: Tarnishing of silver is corrosion by traces of hydrogen sulphide in the atmosphere, which produces a thin black layer of silver sulphide on the surface.

value: Kelvin temperature equals Celsius temperature plus 273
reasoning: The Kelvin scale has the same degree size as the Celsius scale but starts at absolute zero, which is about minus 273 degrees Celsius, so 273 must be added to a Celsius reading to obtain the Kelvin value.
Resistivity is resistance times cross-sectional area divided by length, so its dimensions are resistance times length, giving units of ohm-metre or equivalently ohm-centimetre.

Satellite links use microwaves in the gigahertz range, which belong to the radio part of the spectrum, because these penetrate the ionosphere instead of being reflected by it and are not absorbed by the atmosphere as infrared and ultraviolet are.
Urine formed in the kidney passes down the ureter to be stored in the urinary bladder and is finally voided through the urethra.
The pituitary is a single midline gland lying in a bony hollow at the base of the brain, whereas the adrenals, testes and ovaries all occur as bilateral pairs.

Mitochondria are semi-autonomous organelles carrying their own circular DNA and ribosomes, which lets them make some of their own proteins; the Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and endoplasmic reticulum have no genetic material.
Edward Jenner showed in 1796 that inoculation with material from cowpox protected against smallpox, and this first vaccination introduced the principle of immunization to medicine.
